statement: The task's marine-beach population is limited to the nine Boston Harbor beaches rather than all marine beaches in the annual testing files.
evidence_of_dependence: “I think I should focus on the nine Boston Harbor beaches” and “determine any violations at those specific beach names”.
alternative: The task asks “How many marine beaches” without a Boston Harbor restriction, and the annual files contain other marine beaches, including “333 Commercial Street” in Provincetown.
reason: Restricting the population to nine beaches could exclude most of the beaches eligible for the count.

statement: Every record in each inspected annual file belongs to the year indicated in that file's name.
evidence_of_dependence: The code reads `water-body-testing-{yr}.csv` and labels all resulting counts with `print(yr, ...)` without checking `Year` or `Sample Date`.
reason: Misfiled records would make the year-labelled summaries misleading and could affect later period filtering.

statement: Each beach-name substring selects records belonging only to the intended Boston Harbor beach.
evidence_of_dependence: The agent uses `str.contains(term,case=False,na=False)` to identify target beaches; the `M Street` result includes `Wollaston @ Sachem Street (DCR)`.
alternative: The output shows that the substring `M Street` also matches `Sachem Street`, so a substring match need not identify the intended beach.
reason: Unrelated sampling locations can contaminate a target beach's violation history.

statement: All records for each intended beach can be found using its selected name substring without resolving historical aliases or consulting the beach datasheets.
evidence_of_dependence: The agent searches only `['Constitution','Castle','Pleasure Bay','City Point','M Street','Carson','Malibu','Tenean','Wollaston']` while planning to identify 'all occurrences of violations'.
alternative: The material index includes individual beach datasheets and `boston-harbor-beaches.txt`, which may provide beach identities or sampling-location mappings not captured by these substrings.
reason: An unrecognized alias could hide violations or cause one physical beach to be treated as multiple beaches.

statement: Every marine testing record has a Beach Type Description that becomes exactly 'marine' after lowercasing, without needing whitespace trimming or other normalization.
reason: Other encodings or missing classifications could exclude relevant beaches and their violations.

statement: The annual testing files' Violation field is sufficient to identify all violations relevant to the task without reconciling Indicator Level or the separate beach water-quality datasheets.
evidence_of_dependence: The agent describes 'Identifying beach violations' and summarizes only `x['Violation'].value_counts(dropna=False)`.
alternative: The index also supplies beach-specific 'Bacterial Water Quality' datasheets, and the annual files contain `Organism` and `Indicator Level`, which could bear on interpreting or reconciling violation status.
reason: If violation flags are incomplete or require reconciliation, their counts alone would not establish an uninterrupted safe history.

statement: Every violation in the selected records is encoded as a Violation value that becomes exactly 'yes' after trimming whitespace and lowercasing.
target: v and per-beach violation counts and violation-year summaries
reason: Other affirmative encodings or unresolved missing flags would cause violations to be omitted.

statement: The sampling locations selected under each target term belong to one beach for purposes of the requested beach count.
target: x and per-beach record, year, and violation summaries
evidence_of_dependence: The agent reports one summary for `Constitution` covering five names and one for `Wollaston` covering four names.
reason: Counting sampling locations separately rather than as parts of one beach could change both the counting unit and its safety classification.

statement: All selected testing records are relevant to the swimming seasons in the task, so no Sample Date season filter is necessary.
target: x, v, and per-beach violation counts and violation-year summaries
evidence_of_dependence: The code selects records by beach name and violation flag without filtering `Sample Date`.
alternative: The task specifies 'no violation at all throughout the seasons', which could mean only records within swimming seasons rather than every available test.
reason: If out-of-season tests are present and excluded by the intended definition, their violations could incorrectly disqualify beaches.
